Balloons / chute and hatch / updated 9 September 2026

The Balloons Domain

Float a box
past obstacles

Choose which balloons to release so the box reaches the green height band at low speed, without bursting a balloon.

The original chute and the new hatch combine hidden lift dynamics with tilt and contact.

New: hatch geometry and two mechanical replay videos.
Historical sweep results remain in a separate section.

Version: pybullet_balloons, contact-decoy generation; experiment keys balloons-agent_continual_uniform and balloons-agent_continual_model_free_uniform.
1
Version used in the sweep

What changed from the original puzzle

Transient motion

Drag is 2.2, down from 12. The rising box can overshoot its predicted rest height.

A balloon can burst at the ceiling even when the predicted hover height is inside the band.

Tilt and contact

Balloon attachments are spread across the box top by clip index.

Off-centre pulls can tilt or sway the box into the two chute walls.

Contact challenge

The historical generator searched for alternatives with similar hover heights and different ascent outcomes.

Its early stopping could misclassify an oscillation as a jam. Later audits check sustained contact and full release sequences.

Predicted hover height is a useful filter. It does not certify that the ascent will succeed.

Source: settings.py balloons_drag / balloons_require_jam_decoy; pybullet_balloons_base.py chute and attachment geometry.
2
The scene

The box must pass between two walls

  • The slot is 9.6 cm wide, from z = 0.50 to 1.00 m.
  • Attachment offsets span −2.8 to +2.8 cm, ordered by clip index.
  • Walls collide with the box only. The arm and balloons pass through them.
  • Balanced net pull alone is not a guarantee: the full motion and contacts determine whether the box clears the slot.
Source: pybullet_balloons_base.py, chute_half_gap=0.048, chute_z_lo/hi, attach_span=0.028 and collision filters.

4
Geometry and collision rules

Walls block the box; the ceiling bursts balloons

  • Both chute walls and hatch panels collide with the box only.
  • Balloons and the robot pass through these obstacles. Wall contact does not burst balloons.
  • The hatch opening is offset by 1.2 cm. The payload is 20 × 7 × 3.6 cm.
  • Off-centre balloon pulls rotate the box. Release order changes its path and contacts.

Cross-section schematic, not a trajectory. Balloon bursting is a separate ceiling-height rule.

Source: visible box-wall collision filters and ceiling burst rule in pybullet_balloons_base.py / pybullet_balloons.py.

Same objects and skills, richer motion

Release(robot, clip)

Push the toggle open. Parameters set approach distance and contact height. A freed balloon cannot be clipped back.

Wait(robot)

Hold still while the physics evolves. A jam is not automatically a terminal loss; it can leave the task unsolved.

Source: pybullet_balloons_base.py object types; ground_truth_models/balloons/options.py; sweep observations are noiseless.
9
Hidden dynamics

Height is only the free-ascent prediction

Lc(z) = Lc · max(0, 1 − (z − ztable) / h)
z* = ztable + h · (1 − W / Σ Lc)

W includes the box and freed balloons. The second expression assumes an unconstrained equilibrium; it does not model overshoot or wall contact.

QuantitySweep valueMeaning
Red / blue / green / gold lift0.35 / 0.50 / 0.70 / 1.00 NPer-colour lift at table height
Fade height0.80 mLift declines with height
Pine / oak box mass0.05 / 0.08 kgBoth materials occur in the sweep
Balloon mass / air drag0.005 kg / 2.2Freed mass and transient damping
Ceiling / settle thresholdz = 1.18 m / speed < 0.01 m/sBurst boundary and the evaluator's low-speed check
True constants shown for explanation, not supplied as answers to the agent. Source: settings.py and pybullet_balloons.py hover_height().
10
Historical generator / corrected after the sweep

A predicted rest height does not prove a jam

  1. Draw a rack and box material; enumerate balloon subsets and their unconstrained hover heights.
  2. The sweep's helper could stop at a low-speed turning point before the box finished oscillating.
  3. Later replay showed that some supposed jamming alternatives actually reached the target. The earlier uniqueness and jam labels are not established.
  4. The revised checks execute Release sequences, require sustained off-goal rest, and verify that a suspected jam disappears without wall collisions.

Height alone can favour the wrong subset. Release order and the path through the chute still matter during execution.

Timeouts remain unresolved. A tested reference can win in both orders while an alternative wins in one order and jams in the other.

Source: docs/uncertainty-results/balloons-failure-analysis.md and balloons-subclass-followup.md; historical scores are preserved.

  • Training draws prefer colours and materials not yet shown; generation can fall back to a free draw.

14
Agent interfaces / current MB contract

What the simulator adds

Model-based (MB)

  • Uses a visible base simulator with the scene, chute geometry and rigid-body contacts.
  • Writes a simulator subclass for release, attachment, lift and bursting; explicitly fits physical parameters.
  • Can test release plans in its learned simulator before paying real steps.

Model-free baseline (MF)

  • Has the same real environment, skill tools, observations, journal and recorded experience.
  • Has no supplied simulator or fit-and-rollout workbench.
  • Still has arbitrary Python: it can fit equations and reason about dynamics by hand.

Contact prediction is the intended benefit. The baseline's name does not mean it must guess or cannot build an analytic model.

The historical sweep used the earlier residual interface. Current MB uses the unified subclass contract; historical results are not reruns of it.
